title: Type deduction with pointers, references, and const
recap: Plain auto often drops reference and top-level const qualifications when deducing a new object. auto& explicitly asks to retain reference behavior.
Type deduction syntax is part of the API when callers depend on aliasing. Verify both the deduced type and that writes reach the intended original object.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Practice type deduction with pointers, references, and const.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement selectCounter(first,second,chooseFirst), preserving a modifiable lvalue reference in its deduced return type. chooseFirst selects first when true, otherwise second. The signature uses auto&; returning a value copy would break assignment through the result.
hints: Keep auto& in the return signature.
Return one of the existing reference parameters.
Do not make a plain-auto local copy of the selected integer.
